expectations.text: States plainly that the recent-charge lookup is not sufficient
expectations.evidence: "Why the new check isn't enough: 'Look for a recent charge with the same amount before charging' is check-then-act, not a constraint — it's the same shape of race that caused the original incident"

expectations.text: Identifies the lookup as a check-then-act race rather than a device
expectations.evidence: "it's a check-then-act... TOCTOU race. Two redeliveries (or two worker replicas) can both run the 'any recent charge with this amount?' query, both see nothing, both proceed"

expectations.text: Recommends a required idempotency key on the charge path
expectations.evidence: "Generate a deterministic idempotency key per logical charge (e.g. order_id)... pass it as Stripe's idempotency_key"

expectations.text: Recommends a database unique constraint backing the idempotency key
expectations.evidence: "Add a unique constraint in your own ledger on order_id (or (order_id, idempotency_key)) for successful charges"

expectations.text: Separates the defect from the mistake from the underlying system hazard
expectations.evidence: Lists: Defect (340 charged twice), Mistake (retry called charge again), Hazard (charge() has no idempotency guarantee)

expectations.text: Locates the hazard as a system property rather than as a worker bug or human error
expectations.evidence: "The bug is that your consumer isn't idempotent, which is a precondition for consuming an at-least-once queue at all"

expectations.text: Sweeps for other non-idempotent side effects reachable from a retry
expectations.evidence: "any other queue consumer in this system that isn't idempotent (order confirmation emails, webhooks, ledger writes, inventory decrements) has the identical failure mode"

expectations.text: Treats 'second time this happened' as evidence for pushing to a Control-rung device
expectations.evidence: Acknowledges 'second time' but uses it to motivate class sweep; does not explicitly connect recurrence as diagnostic evidence for rung-level choice (Detection vs. Control)

expectations.text: Attributes cause to the system, not to any person
expectations.evidence: "The bug is that your consumer isn't idempotent" — system design property
